entries.source:
Core strategy: Invests in a productive colony and technology before committing substantial attacks. Prioritized construction projects build up its settlement; development, military infrastructure and time increase war readiness.

Economy and development: Studies hydration, food-source growth, obstacles and worker reach. Manages food expansion, upgrades and defenses alongside production.

Attack and defense: Estimates healthy warriors' attack power and begins strikes when power or timing conditions are met. Favors previously seen, accessible buildings, especially barracks and schools, and moves its attack flags toward valuable targets.

Compared with other AIs: More deliberate about terrain and target value than Numbi. More patient than Warrush, trading early pressure for a developed base and stronger troops.

Strengths and weaknesses: Broad infrastructure planning and valuable military targets give its strikes purpose. Preparation takes time, allowing faster opponents to contest resources before its main force is ready.

Counterplay to try: Contest expansion early. Protect barracks and schools as well as food, and keep a reserve when attacking its developed settlement.

entries.source:
Core strategy: Uses reactive priorities to grow a working economy and turn spare labor into food, technology and military pressure. Its normal policy is rule-based; learned-policy experiments require separate configuration.

Economy and development: Adjusts worker production to staffing demand and keeps births going. Food trouble suppresses expansion and technology spending. Adds swimming when water access materially helps.

Attack and defense: Prepares attacks using observed enemy technology and available troops. Water-crossing campaigns need swimming-capable warriors. Supports long campaigns with forward inns and hospitals, and can stage forces before advancing.

Commitment and emergencies: Holds an offensive through minor harassment instead of repeatedly marching home. Serious attacks can recall defenders. Early emergencies can trigger warrior-only production and a hospital; famine can trigger a smaller desperation attack.

Compared with other AIs: More concerned with forward support than Warrush. Maxima goes further in budgeting sustainable births, training and deployment against estimated enemy strength.

Strengths and weaknesses: Connects pressure to food, healing and reachability. Forward infrastructure must stay supplied, and continued births can keep pressure on limited food. Emergency priorities force tradeoffs between growth and survival.

Counterplay to try: Contest forward inns, hospitals and food sources. Keep defenders together against its push; minor harassment may not persuade it to retreat.

Scouting: Uses discovered enemy buildings and observed enemy troops.

معیشت اور ترقی: عملے کی ضرورت کے مطابق کارکنوں کی پیداوار بدلتا اور پیدائشیں جاری رکھتا ہے۔ خوراک کی مشکلات توسیع اور ٹیکنالوجی کے اخراجات کم کرتی ہیں۔ جہاں پانی تک رسائی سے نمایاں فائدہ ہو، وہاں تیراکی کی تربیت شامل کرتا ہے۔

حملہ اور دفاع: دشمن کی دیکھی گئی ٹیکنالوجی اور دستیاب فوج کے مطابق حملوں کی تیاری کرتا ہے۔ پانی عبور کرنے والی مہموں کے لیے تیرنے والے جنگجو ضروری ہیں۔ اگلے مورچوں پر سرائے اور ہسپتال بنا کر طویل مہموں کو سہارا دیتا ہے اور پیش قدمی سے پہلے فوج جمع کر سکتا ہے۔

Core strategy: Combines growth, training, upgrades and warfare through overlapping conditions. Can attack while expanding, and redirect economic effort toward recovery when feeding fails.

Opening: The shipped aggressive profile begins war preparation at five total units and permits war at five warriors, counting level-zero warriors too. Aims for three attack flags with five warriors each. Custom strategy files can change these thresholds.

Economy and development: Expands food and birth capacity, trains workers, develops swimming and movement, and upgrades buildings. Adjusts food staffing, responds to starvation and pursues fruit.

Attack and defense: Samples reachable enemy buildings for attacks. Can use clearing flags to open resource-blocked routes. Defensive flags cover clusters of threatened units and buildings. Later, trained ground-attacking explorers target enemy unit groups.

Compared with other AIs: Shares Warrush's early aggression but has more follow-through. Unlike Cabino, does not consistently prioritize hospitals and inns.

Strengths and weaknesses: Broad tactical coverage combines early pressure with continued development. Random target selection can spend effort on less valuable buildings. Its thresholds do not provide Maxima's detailed estimate of opposing fighting power.

Counterplay to try: Expect an early attack. Protect food and workers, contest expansion, and prepare for explorer attacks if it reaches advanced training.

Core strategy: Builds food and population first, adds healing, science and training, then shifts toward warfare. Its broad phases advance with time rather than with the opponent's progress.

Economy and development: Scales building demand with population and estimates nearby food sources. Later phases add upgrades, defenses and expansion to support its growing army.

Attack and defense: Attacks when enough healthy fighters exist or a timeout expires. Places war flags on sampled enemy buildings. When its fighting force falls too low, removes attack flags and raises the thresholds for another attempt.

Compared with other AIs: More predictable than Castor or Nicowar. Castor considers terrain and target value more carefully; Nicowar applies pressure much earlier.

Strengths and weaknesses: Broad supporting infrastructure can make it dangerous after an uninterrupted buildup, but its timetable may not match the battle. Simple target selection and longer pauses after losses make its attacks easier to anticipate.

Counterplay to try: Apply pressure before its military phase. Grow food and training behind your attacks, and exploit the pause after defeating an assault.

Scouting: Its attack routine reads enemy building positions directly without a visibility check.

entries.source:
Core strategy: Attacks before opponents finish a long economic or technological buildup. Expects combat to decide the game before a large support network becomes necessary.

Economy and development: Once six units can harvest, sets production to four workers, one explorer and three warriors. Adds barracks as training fills up, but restricts new inns. Spare construction often goes toward hospitals and movement training.

Attack and defense: Marks discovered enemy buildings with guard areas so warriors apply continuing pressure. Does not wait for a carefully assembled wave. Clears obstructing resources and protects some renewable sources.

Fruit policy: Forbids fruit harvesting, avoiding fruit-related armor penalties and declining Econo's conversion strategy.

Compared with other AIs: More committed to early pressure than Numbi or Castor. Nicowar also opens aggressively, but follows through with a broader upgrade and tactical program.

Strengths and weaknesses: Punishes slow openings and forces early defensive spending. Limited systematic upgrading and lean food support make a stalled offensive costly. Terrain and long journeys can erode its early advantage.

Counterplay to try: Protect inns and swarms early. Replace workers as well as defenders, develop training, then counterattack once its rush loses momentum.

Scouting: Opening exploration flags use enemy starting locations directly. Later attack-area placement requires visibility.

Core strategy: Shares unit production among construction, upgrades, defense, attacks and exploration. Separate managers request and reserve units, developing economy and military together.

Economy and development: Builds and upgrades a broad settlement, manages inn and tower staffing, clears building surroundings and protects renewable resources. Scouts fruit and advertises food to compete for converts.

Attack and defense: Chooses an enemy and prioritizes hospitals, then inns, then barracks. Supports up to four attacks, generally assigning eight to twenty warriors per target according to availability and nearby enemies. Uses separate defensive flags around threatened buildings.

Training: Requires enough suitable warriors and a completed barracks to attack, but does not wait for maximum technology. Continued upgrades and training strengthen later attacks.

Compared with other AIs: More purposeful about dismantling support buildings than Nicowar. Spreads attacks more than Maxima's gathered waves, using unit reservations to manage competing demands.

Strengths and weaknesses: Combines growth, training, defense and several attacks. Destroying food and healing can weaken an entire colony. Random opponent selection and fixed building priorities may miss opportunities; multiple attacks can divide its force.

Counterplay to try: Defend hospitals and inns. Contest exposed expansion and concentrate defenders against individual attacks. Damage food or training before it sustains several fronts.

Scouting: Its attack selector reads enemy building lists without an explicit visibility check. Some economic comparisons use enemy statistics directly.

entries.source:
Core strategy: Treats food, workers, births, training, construction and combat as competing demands. Sizes its army partly against estimated enemy strength, then tries to deliver that army effectively.

Economy and development: Budgets births against food and labor, preserves idle opportunities for training, and stops adding surplus workers when military production is needed. Scales training capacity and avoids taking too much infrastructure offline for upgrades.

Scouting and decisions: Estimates enemy forces from visible units and remembered sightings using a fitted model. Targets depend on value, distance, towers, exposed workers and persistence. Fruit missions support food variety and conversion.

Attack and defense: Reserves warriors for training and defense, then gathers eligible land forces near friendly food infrastructure before launching waves. Uses local defensive responses and evaluates approaches to the colony.

When attacks stall: After four consecutive wave-delivery failures, switches to continuously reinforced attack flags. Amphibious attacks can also use continuous reinforcement. This fallback does not solve every blockage before a rally can form.

Compared with other AIs: Integrates food, training, intelligence and deployment more tightly. Cabino emphasizes several building attacks; Maxima emphasizes estimated demand and delivering gathered forces.

Strengths and weaknesses: Sustains growth and military replacement while adapting to food pressure and observed threats. Needs food, training capacity and open gathering space; congestion and long routes can undermine delivery.

Counterplay to try: Contest exposed food sources, inns and barracks before waves gather. Keep a supplied defensive force together and disrupt reinforcement routes. Expect repeated pressure after the first wave.

Scouting: Force estimates use sightings and observation history, rather than hidden enemy troop totals.

خوبیاں اور کمزوریاں: خوراک کے دباؤ اور دیکھی گئی دھمکیوں کے مطابق بدلتے ہوئے آبادی کی بڑھوتری اور فوجی نقصانات کی تلافی جاری رکھتا ہے۔ اسے خوراک، تربیتی گنجائش اور جمع ہونے کے لیے کھلی جگہ چاہیے؛ ہجوم اور لمبے راستے فوج کی ترسیل خراب کر سکتے ہیں۔

آزمانے کے لیے مقابلے کا طریقہ: لہریں جمع ہونے سے پہلے کھلے خوراکی ذرائع، سراؤں اور بیرکوں کو چیلنج کریں۔ رسد پانے والے محافظ اکٹھے رکھیں اور کمک کے راستے توڑیں۔ پہلی لہر کے بعد بھی بار بار دباؤ کی توقع رکھیں۔
